subject: POC launch playbook, checkpoints, and accountability
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@arcadiamed.com>, Devon Hart <devon.hart@arcadiamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC launch playbook, checkpoints, and accountability

Thanks again for the time today — great alignment on the core use cases and success drivers. Quick post-call recap and a proposed lightweight launch playbook so we can lock dates and owners.

Key outcomes from discovery:
- Goal: validate integration of Redwood inference into Arcadia’s clinical notes pipeline for assistive summarization and triage (pilot cohort: 3 hospitals).
- Success criteria (business + technical):
  1) Clinical acceptability: >85% of sampled summaries rated "useful" by clinician panel (blind review).
  2) Performance: p95 inference latency <200ms for 512-token requests at expected pilot concurrency.
  3) Cost guardrail: projected token cost for pilot <= $8k/month (est. 250k tokens/day).
  4) Security: SOC2 evidence and VPC/private deployment acceptable to Arcadia security.

Proposed minimal POC playbook (3-week rolling cadence):
- Week 0 (Prep): contract/MAP sign, data access path established (SFTP or secure API), acceptance test set finalized.
- Week 1 (Integrate): model integration, wiring of KV cache, initial smoke tests.
- Week 2 (Validation sprints): three focused validation runs against prioritized prompt set + clinician review.
- Week 3 (Readout): consolidated results, risk register, and go/no-go recommendation.

Owners / responsibilities (initial):
- Executive sponsor / commercial: Alyssa Turner (Arcadia) / Logan Wright (Redwood).
- POC program manager: Marissa Cole (Redwood) — scheduling, SLAs, stakeholder cadence.
- Infra / integration: Monica Patel (Redwood) — deployment, perf tuning, quantization profiles.
- Arcadia technical lead: Devon Hart — data mapping and clinician review coordination.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Alyssa/Devon: confirm pilot start week windows (we suggested week of 10/19 or 10/26).
2) Arcadia security: share the SOC2 report or preferred security questionnaire (we can push ours too).
3) Marissa: drop a draft schedule and mutual action plan (MAP) by EOD tomorrow.
4) Monica: prepare an acceptance-test template (latency, accuracy sample, and API conformance).

Attachments: I’ll upload a draft MAP and a preliminary schedule — see attached poc-schedule-v1.xlsx and mutual-action-plan.pdf.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff once we have confirmed dates.

—
Logan Wright
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
log.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0184
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@arcadiamed.com>

Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC launch playbook, checkpoints, and accountability

Logan — thanks for the crisp recap. This aligns with our expectations. A few quick notes: 

- Week windows: 10/19 looks tight for legal sign-off; can we target 10/26 as preferred, 11/2 as backup?
- Security: our InfoSec needs the SOC2 and a short answers doc on data residency & retention. I looped in Devon (technical lead) to coordinate the data transfer approach.
- Clinician panel: we’ll line up 5 reviewers and provide a blinded scoring template; can Marissa include that in the MAP?

One ask from our side: can Redwood provide a minimum viable acceptance-test checklist (latency, token accounting, examples of failure modes) — that will help our procurement decision.

If 10/26 works we’ll schedule the kickoff for the week — thanks for being flexible.

Best,
Alyssa
VP, Product Strategy — Arcadia Medical
alyssa.turner@arcadiamed.com | (617) 555-2246

Subject: Re: POC launch playbook, checkpoints, and accountability — Draft schedule & MAP

Alyssa / team — attaching the draft MAP and a pivotable POC schedule (see poc-schedule-v1.xlsx and mutual-action-plan.pdf). Highlights and commitments: 

Draft schedule (summary):
- Kickoff (30m): Mon 10/26 10:00 PT — alignment, environment access, and acceptance criteria sign-off.
- Integration week (10/26–10/30): environment provisioning (Mon), API wiring (Tue–Wed), smoke tests (Thu).
- Validation sprint week (11/2–11/6): run three validation windows with clinician review cycles + perf tuning.
- Readout (11/09): 45-min readout with exec summary and raw results.

Mutual action items (owners & SLAs):
- Arcadia: provide sample data subset and clinician scoring rubric by 10/20 — owner: Devon.
- Redwood: provision private test endpoint and baseline model by 10/23 — owner: Monica.
- Arcadia: sign MAP and NDA (if needed) by 10/22 — owner: Alyssa.
- Redwood: deliver acceptance-tests.csv template and runbook by 10/23 — owner: Marissa.

Acceptance criteria (operationalized in acceptance-tests.csv):
- Latency: p95 <200ms for 75th percentile request size; no >500ms tail spikes during 1-hour sustained run.
- Quality: blind clinician scoring median >=4 on 1–5 scale for usefulness.
- Stability: <2% error rate over validation runs and successful KV cache warmup within first 50 queries.

Contingencies / gating: if latency or error rate exceed thresholds during validation sprint, we trigger an immediate tuning window (2 business days) and schedule a secondary validation run. If issues persist, we’ll surface a mitigation plan and pause expansion beyond the pilot cohort.

I’ll create calendar invites for the kickoff and weekly check-ins (Thu 11:00 PT) once Alyssa confirms 10/26.

—
Marissa Cole
POC Program Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC launch playbook, checkpoints, and accountability — infra & acceptance tests

Devon / Alyssa — quick infra note:

- We can stand up a private test endpoint in your VPC using our Private deployment connector; estimate provisioning ~48 hours once network peering is approved.
- For perf parity, I’ll start with a 8-gpu reserved pool with continuous batching on short seqs; we’ll tune quantization to MQA int8 if you accept slight accuracy trade-offs.
- Attached acceptance-tests.csv contains: request sample id, payload size, expected p95 latency threshold, clinician sample id, scoring rubric pointer, and token accounting sample. Please populate the clinician sample ids before 10/20.

Quick ask: Devon, can you confirm whether SFTP or presigned S3 is preferred for the sample payloads? SFTP requires opening port access in the pilot subnet.

One-line confirmation from me: 10/26 kickoff works from our side — we’ll aim to have the private endpoint by 10/23 if Arcadia approves network steps this week.

—
Monica Patel
Infra & Integrations, Redwood Inference
